Definition: a seer (as often rendered); but also (abstractly) a vision
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses rôʼeh for a seer (as often rendered); but also (abstractly) a vision. In 1 Samuel 9:9, we read, "…seer: for now a Prophet was beforetime called…"; in Isaiah 28:7, "…way through strong drink; they err in vision…". You hear it again in 1 Samuel 9:11 — "…found young maidens going out to draw water…" — and in 1 Samuel 9:18, "…Saul drew near to Samuel in the gate…".
TheologicalSignificance: I hold rôʼeh close because it is part of how Scripture speaks plainly about real life. And I believe rôʼeh still speaks to us today, because God's word does not go out of date.
